baseline_models.focus_anchor: The plural burial places at word 2 are the patient of the passive overturning verb at word 3.
baseline_models.mechanism: Earth is turned away from burial enclosures and what they concealed is stirred up and brought out. The passive construction foregrounds the collapse of containment and the emergence of occupants rather than the acting agent.

activation_trace.role: The burial-place branch supplies resting enclosures together with the dead placed inside them.
The upturned-earth branch supplies extraction of concealed contents and makes release the verb's operative result.

changed_reading.after: Burial enclosures are forcibly turned open so that their concealed occupants emerge.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The inward, hidden possibilities of the grave root at word 2 meet the bottom-to-top inversion of the verb at word 3.
baseline_models.mechanism: A grave is an inward and potentially sealed geometry, not merely a location. Turning a container's underside into its upper side reverses that geometry: interior becomes exposed surface and what was low becomes manifest.

activation_trace.role: The hidden, sunken, and sealed-inward branch supplies the protected interior whose orientation can be reversed.
The demolished basin with bottom made top supplies a literal topology of inversion rather than simple opening.

changed_reading.before: The covers over graves are removed.
changed_reading.after: The grave's spatial logic is inverted: depth becomes surface and protected interior becomes exterior.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Plural graves at word 2 combine with the verb's branch of scattering possessions and turning them over one another at word 3.
baseline_models.mechanism: The grave field partitions people into discrete resting places. The disorder branch of the verb allows the event to destroy not only covers but compartmental arrangement, converting separate deposits into an exposed, disordered aggregate.

activation_trace.role: The burial and cemetery scope supplies a plurality of separately placed deposits.
The scattered-belongings branch supplies loss of partition and ordered placement among exposed contents.

changed_reading.before: Each grave is opened as a separate unit.
changed_reading.after: The cemetery's partitioned order fails, leaving formerly separated contents turned out into disorder.

context_deltas.mechanism: The preceding signs repeat a progression of cover, arrangement, and reservoir losing integrity. Grave-overturning becomes the innermost human-scale instance of the same operation: a containing layer can no longer keep its contents hidden or ordered.

activation_trace.role: The hidden, inward enclosure supplies the final and most intimate container in the sequence.
The extraction of buried contents supplies the human-scale release produced when that container fails.
The overhead covering supplies the largest enclosing layer in the opening sequence.
Opening by fissure supplies failure of the upper boundary.
Casting items apart supplies loss of ordered placement and activates the focus verb's dispersive branch.
The water-gathering land supplies a reservoir boundary that holds contents together.
Wide splitting with emission supplies pressure-driven release from the reservoir.

structural_cues: Ayat 82:1-4 repeat the same conditional frame and passive event profile.
The sequence moves from an overhead cover through celestial arrangement and gathered water to burial interiors.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a cover that cracks, lights cast apart, gathered water released, and hidden graves upturned. I infer a scale-descending container-failure sequence ending at human enclosure; a live alternative is four parallel signs with no nested spatial relation.

changed_reading.before: Graves undergo an isolated cemetery event.
changed_reading.after: Grave-opening is the inward terminal stage of world-scale unhousing, where each layer loses the power to contain and order what is inside.

context_deltas.mechanism: The verb's image of possessions turned over one another acquires a temporal counterpart. What had been separated as advanced and deferred is made co-present, and overturning the hidden enclosure becomes the condition for a self to encounter the whole sequence at once.

activation_trace.role: The hidden inward store supplies a temporal compartment in which earlier and later material had ceased to be visible.
The turning of possessions over one another supplies simultaneous exposure and collapse of their prior ordering.
Disclosure to a knower supplies the cognitive result of the physical unsealing.
Forward precedence supplies one side of the sequence that had ordered a life's acts.
Deferral to a later time supplies the complementary temporal compartment now exposed with the first.

structural_cues: Ayah 82:5 follows the four repeated conditional openings as their cognitive consequence.
Its final two verbs form an explicit earlier-later opposition.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies physical disorder, disclosure, and the opposed categories of advancing and delaying. I infer that the grave functions as a time-sealed store whose turnover makes separated acts co-present; the live alternative is that only bodies emerge and knowledge follows independently.

changed_reading.before: The grave gives back a body located in space.
changed_reading.after: The overturned grave also gives back a life as a temporal heap, with what went ahead and what lagged behind exposed together to its self.

context_deltas.mechanism: Scattering and bottom-to-top inversion are read against a measured sequence of making, completing, balancing, forming, and assembling the human. The grave event therefore resembles the controlled inverse of composition: a made whole is opened down to its arrangement rather than simply erased.

activation_trace.role: The resting place of the dead locates the composed human whole at the point where inversion acts.
The disordered turning of items supplies separation of a former arrangement into exposed components.
The bottom-to-top inversion supplies a reversible spatial operation rather than disappearance.
Measurement and proportion supply an intentional specification behind the human composite.
Intrinsic straightness and completion supply the achieved integrity that overturning interrupts.
Setting a thing upright supplies the balancing operation within the original construction.
Determinate form supplies the visible configuration of the composed whole.
Fitting one thing into another supplies the assembly operation whose inverse the focus event can expose.

structural_cues: Ayat 82:7-8 address one human through a sequence of making, proportioning, balancing, forming, and assembling verbs.
The focus verb is passive, allowing its apparent disorder to remain under an unstated controlling agency.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an intentionally assembled form and an event of scattering and inversion. I infer that the inverse operation can expose components under the same formative authority and potentially prepare recomposition; the live alternative is that the formation sequence only recalls first creation and supplies no process claim about the grave.

changed_reading.before: Grave-overturning is random destruction of what burial held.
changed_reading.after: Grave-overturning can be carried as the inverse of composition, opening a measured human arrangement without implying that its maker has lost command of the parts.

context_deltas.mechanism: The concealed grave and the already guarded written account become two storage systems brought into alignment. Extracting what was hidden is no longer only bodily emergence; it is the material opening of a life whose acts have been preserved for reckoning.

activation_trace.role: The sealed inward state supplies a material archive unavailable to ordinary sight.
Extraction of concealed contents supplies the transition from storage to inspectability.
Accounting and recompense supply the procedure for which concealed material becomes relevant.
Guarding and continuous care supply preservation against loss before disclosure.
Ordered inscription supplies a legible counterpart to the focus event's material exposure.
The production of acts supplies the subject matter preserved and eventually exposed.

structural_cues: Ayat 82:10-12 move from guardians to writers to the acts being known.
The accounting cue appears immediately before that preservation-and-writing sequence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies accounting, vigilant preservation, writing, acts, and extraction of hidden contents. I infer that bodily unsealing and documentary disclosure are synchronized views of one life becoming inspectable; the live alternative is that the record is sufficient and entirely independent of physical exhumation.

changed_reading.before: The graves release their physical occupants.
changed_reading.after: The graves open as material evidence stores, making buried lives inspectable alongside the preserved account of what they did.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later negation of absence activates the grave as a special case of hiddenness. Overturning is therefore a change of state from being withdrawn from sight to being inescapably present, not merely movement of remains from one location to another.

activation_trace.role: The hidden and sunken state supplies burial as withdrawal from ordinary visibility.
Bringing concealed contents out supplies the transition that cancels withdrawal.
Being screened from eyes supplies the general state that the later negation refuses.
The root's explicit burial branch links absence directly back to the focus enclosure.

structural_cues: Ayah 82:16 uses an emphatically negated plural state of absence.
The context root inventory itself joins visual withdrawal and grave burial.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies burial as hiddenness, extraction as disclosure, and a later refusal of absence. I infer that the focus event is the operation by which absence is revoked; the live alternative is that 82:16 refers only to inability to escape a later condition.

changed_reading.before: Buried persons are moved out of graves.
changed_reading.after: Burial's apparent absence is itself cancelled: those withdrawn from sight become unavoidably present.

context_deltas.mechanism: A grave is the last discrete enclosure around an individual self, while the focus verb can scatter what had been held as possessions. The closing removal of self-to-self disposal turns that physical breach into a social and legal one: neither enclosure, property, nor proxy control remains operative.

activation_trace.role: The sealed inward branch supplies a private boundary around each buried self.
The scattering of held belongings supplies loss of controlled possession when the boundary fails.
The thing itself or self supplies the two discrete identities between which proxy agency is denied.
The definite object of knowledge and predication supplies the unrestricted item over which control fails.
Ownership and power of disposal supply the agency explicitly withdrawn at the sequence's close.
Sovereign authority supplies the control that remains after private and proxy control disappear.

structural_cues: Ayah 82:19 repeats self against self, negates control over anything, and then relocates authority.
The plural graves spatially individuate the selves before their enclosures are overturned.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies sealed identities, scattered holdings, denial of ownership between selves, and remaining sovereignty. I infer that spatial unsealing enacts withdrawal of private control and proxy substitution; the live alternative is a purely physical grave event followed by a separate statement about agency.

changed_reading.after: The last private enclosures are abolished, and the exposed selves and contents stand beyond ownership, transfer, or proxy control.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it lets a remote vessel-lid branch of generosity and a shining-deception branch recode burial as a tolerated cover. It remains valid as an activation because the focus itself supplies sealed inwardness and bottom-to-top inversion. Downstream prose should present it only as an analogy triggered by 82:6, not as the lexical meaning of the divine epithet or as a claim that generosity itself deceives.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The grave's sealed-inward branch at word 2 and the verb's container-inversion branch at word 3 can support the temporary-lid geometry.

activation_trace.role: The enclosed, sunken state supplies a cover that can be mistaken for permanent sealing.
Inverting a container supplies the eventual expiry and reversal of that cover.
A surface that attracts by appearing stable supplies the mistaken inference that concealment will last.
The remote lid-over-vessel image supplies the material analogy of a generous covering that is real but not final.

changed_reading.before: Burial is a final and permanent cover.
changed_reading.after: Burial can be imagined as a granted lid or interval whose apparent permanence misleads until the container is inverted.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This legal-material reading is surprising because it treats the cemetery event like settlement of an estate. It remains anchored through the focus verb's literal belongings branch and is activated by debt, binding record, property, and authority cues. Downstream prose should qualify it as a cross-domain mechanism, not translate the grave as an estate or reduce the broader accounting term to financial debt.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The burial place at word 2 contains a person, while the belongings-disorder branch at word 3 permits the image of a sealed holding emptied for inspection.

activation_trace.role: The dead person's resting enclosure supplies the sealed estate-like unit.
Scattering belongings supplies the concrete inventory emptied from the unit.
Financial liability supplies the settlement relation applied to the exposed inventory.
A binding inscription that entails judgment supplies enforceable registration of liability.
Property and disposal supply the ordinary control that no longer governs the emptied holding.
Sole authority supplies the jurisdiction under which the nontransferable settlement occurs.

changed_reading.before: The grave is opened to recover its occupant.
changed_reading.after: The grave resembles a sealed estate emptied into view, with holdings and liabilities exposed for settlement under authority the former holder cannot exercise.

strongest_changes: The isolated exhumation became the innermost stage of a scale-descending failure of covers, arrangements, reservoirs, and graves.
Physical overturning became temporal and evidentiary disclosure: a buried life and its advanced or deferred acts become co-present and inspectable.
Burial ceased to signify durable absence or private control; overturning revokes hiddenness and exposes selves beyond proxy disposal.
summary.what_was_special: The focus verb keeps extraction, belongings-disorder, and bottom-to-top inversion live at once. Context routes those branches into physical, temporal, compositional, evidentiary, and legal mechanisms without requiring them to collapse into one final reading.
remaining_uncertainties: It remains unclear whether dispersal and inversion apply primarily to grave structures, their occupants, their associated contents, or all three.
The formation sequence supports an inverse-composition reading, but its use as preparation for recomposition is a reader-supplied possibility rather than an explicit process statement.
The debt, lid, and estate activations are coherent cross-domain models but remain more branch-distant than the enclosure, disclosure, and revoked-absence readings.
